decision.answer: The claim is accurate on the available evidence, with “rocket” referring to the reusable first-stage booster, not the entire rocket.[E22][E16][E11] The video shows the booster upright on a coastal land pad after landing, and its commentary describes a smooth landing and the booster’s eighth landing.[E16][E11] External reporting from Space.com records the Transporter-2 launch and successful booster landing, consistent with the video.[E22] “Nails” is supported as an informal description of success, not a measured assessment of landing accuracy or vehicle condition.[E16][E11] Exact correspondence with an original SpaceX recording was not verified, and the sampled images alone do not establish uninterrupted descent through touchdown.[E15][E16]

The title is broadly accurate about wildfire evacuation and road clearance, but “clear debris” is misleadingly vague: the reported obstructions were abandoned vehicles.[E23]

ABC7 reports that drivers fleeing the Palisades Fire abandoned cars on Sunset Boulevard and that a fire bulldozer pushed them aside to give fire crews access.[E23] The supplied video's sampled frames show a Los Angeles County Fire Department bulldozer among tightly packed vehicles on a smoke-filled road, consistent with that account.[E15][E17][E18]

The evidence does not establish the video's exact filming date or location, an exact match to the externally reported footage, multiple bulldozers, or residents visibly evacuating simultaneously with clearance.[E23][E15][E17][E18] Speech recognition found no recognized speech, so it provides no spoken confirmation of the title; this does not prove speech is absent.[E11]

The claim is false as a description of the supplied video: its reporting says the FAA required SpaceX to investigate the explosion, while the restriction concerned further flights.[E11]

The automated audio transcript identifies the seventh test flight and describes an FAA-required investigation and grounding pending investigation; transcription errors remain possible.[E11] The visible caption reads “BLAST TRIGGERS FLIGHT DELAYS; FAA INVESTIGATING,” consistent with that reporting.[E4]

External evidence also weighs against the claim: Astronomy reports that the FAA permitted Flight 8 in March 2025 while SpaceX’s inquiry into January’s Flight 7 anomalies was still underway, distinguishing launch authorization from permission to investigate.[E24] However, that article principally concerns Flight 12, and its requirements for that flight cannot establish the original Flight 7 requirements.[E24] The Space.com and CNN reports concern Flight 8, so they do not independently verify instructions for the incident in this video.[E25][E26]

The original FAA Flight 7 directive and its exact conditions were not verified from first-hand sources.[E24] The precise incidents covered by Yahoo and substantive supporting excerpts from the FLYING and Yahoo articles were not established, so those sources cannot resolve the remaining uncertainty.[E22][E23]

The examined frame shows the person on the aircraft stairs with arms lowered while uniformed personnel salute; it establishes no returned salute at that instant, not intention or conduct throughout the video.[E12]

The first investigation reported that Fox News covered criticism of Harris and U.S. News reported the Pentagon’s position that vice presidents need not return military salutes; the underlying Pentagon statement was not independently examined, and those articles were not re-examined in the follow-up.[E14][E15]

“Disgraceful” is an opinion; deliberate refusal and the alleged dislike remain not determinable from this evidence.[E12][E15]

The boarding person’s identity, recording date, correspondence with the reported event, and original posting timestamp remain unverified; sampled images also cannot establish the complete video’s actions, speech or on-screen text.[E12][E14][E15]

The C-SPAN material concerns border responsibilities, while the DVIDS page identifies a March 23, 2021 Pentagon briefing but supplies no examined statement resolving the salute question.[E16][E17]

The video's narration portrays the campaign as a prank and urges viewers to vote for Hillary Clinton; sampled visuals include a seated office address and a campaign-cap shopping page.[E11][E19][E22] The external ABC/Jimmy Kimmel page explicitly describes a 2016 April Fools segment assembled from Trump coverage with a voice pretending to be Trump, supporting the comedy interpretation.[E28]

Exact audiovisual correspondence with the original broadcast and the supplied April 1, 2016 upload date were not independently verified; the conclusion concerns this video's purported revelation, not the campaign's private intentions.[E28][E11]

The claim is false for the scheduled opening discussed in the video: Matt Goss discusses a postponement, not confirmation that the residency would start unchanged. [E11][E20][E21]

The broadcast identifies its guest as singer-songwriter Matt Goss and explicitly states that Adele postponed her Las Vegas shows just 24 hours before the first scheduled performance. [E17][E14][E18] The automated speech transcript likewise records Goss discussing postponement; his reference to the first show being intended for that night describes the planned opening, not confirmation it would proceed. [E11]

External reporting corroborates the postponement: BBC News reports that Adele postponed the entire residency and quotes her saying, “I'm so sorry, but my show ain't ready.” [E20] PinkNews also reports the postponement 24 hours before opening night. [E21]

This conclusion concerns that planned opening, not subsequent residency schedules; the speech evidence is automated transcription, and the particular video file was not authenticated against an original broadcast. [E11][E20][E21]

The claim is false as a description of this video: its report concerns Pennsylvania voters reacting to a comedian’s remarks about Puerto Rico at a Trump rally, not Florida residents reacting to Biden’s climate-change remarks. [E11][E16]

The visible location label says “ALLENTOWN, PA,” and the headline reads “PA VOTERS ON "PUERTO RICO" MOMENT AT TRUMP RALLY.” [E15][E18] The audio transcript likewise concerns demands for an apology and voter reactions to that controversy. [E11]

The external White House records examined document Biden campaign remarks at Hillsborough Community College in Tampa, Florida; they establish a different event context and do not substantiate the supplied video’s title. [E20][E21]

This conclusion concerns the title’s mismatch with the supplied footage; it does not establish whether Florida residents ever reacted to Biden’s climate remarks, and the external records examined do not establish this video’s original source or publication date. [E11][E20][E21]

The claim is supported as a historical account, but the specific video’s attribution is only provisionally confirmed.[E20][E23] Vintage Everyday identifies Gladys Ingle as a member of the 13 Black Cats and describes her changing planes to replace a lost wheel in January 1926; Laughing Squid also attributes the transfer and wheel replacement to Ingle.[E20][E23] The San Diego Air & Space Museum independently documents the team’s existence around 1925.[E24]

The supplied footage is consistent with that account: at 68.8 seconds, a person stands on an aircraft wing near another biplane, and at 123.88 seconds, a person is positioned at the landing gear.[E16][E9] These sampled images do not independently establish the person’s identity or show the complete continuous transfer.[E16][E9]

The footage was not matched to an archival original, and the stated posting date, 2007-07-29, remains unverified; the external accounts support the historical event rather than that upload date.[E20][E23]

The claim is false as a description of the reported announcement: external reports describe the Met beginning investigations into Downing Street and Whitehall events, reversing the title’s assertion that investigations had ended. [E15][E16][E17]

Manchester Evening News attributes to Cressida Dick an announcement that the Met was investigating a number of events during the preceding two years for potential Covid-regulation breaches; iNews and HuffPost likewise report investigations beginning. [E17][E18][E19]

The supplied video frames show a televised London Assembly statement with BBC News graphics headed “Downing Street parties”; the visible caption reads “Cressida Dick: we understand deep public concern,” which does not establish that investigations ended. [E5][E9]

The actual spoken wording and its timestamps remain undetermined because transcription failed, so whether this particular video’s soundtrack supports the title cannot be determined; the verdict concerns the externally reported announcement, not later investigative status. [E17][E15][E16]

The claim is misleading as a description of this video: external reporting confirms the Ambassador Bridge reopened after police cleared protesters, while the video describes continuing disruption and diverted traffic.[E21][E17][E11]

The video's speech concerns ongoing protests and a blockade, not an announcement of reopening or mandates ending.[E11] Sampled images show reporting amid stationary trucks, with no identifiable celebration of mandates ending; this visual finding applies only to the sampled moments.[E7][E16]

The reopening itself is supported, but the evidence obtained does not establish that Covid-19 mandates ended at that time or that truckers celebrated their ending.[E21][E17][E11] The crossing's precise ranking as North America's busiest was not independently verified.[E21][E17]

The claim is not verifiable from the evidence obtained: neither the examined video frames nor the external pages establish a giant anaconda becoming trapped while trying to eat a chicken. [E15][E19][E20][E21]

At 19.786 seconds, the video shows a long, dark, snake-like form beside black netting, a blue cylindrical object and upright stakes in muddy water; this does not establish species, measured size, attempted feeding or whether it is stuck. [E15]

The video displays “Courtesy: Cambodia Daily Life,” “Smart Boy” and “No Audio,” and ends with Snopes.com branding; these labels do not verify the incident. [E12][E16] Speech analysis returned no transcribed speech supporting the claim. [E11]

The external material obtained consists of Dailymotion player-navigation text, a Cambodia travel article and material about a fictional cartoon rooster, providing no corroboration of the alleged event. [E19][E20][E21] Whether the Dailymotion candidate matches the supplied video is not determinable because its footage was not compared. [E19]

The sampled visuals do not establish the complete action, and the supplied posting date, 2020-11-20, was not independently verified. [E12][E15]

The claim is misleading: the evidence supports the spread of protests inspired by Canada’s Freedom Convoy, not a verified worldwide decline in public support for vaccine mandates and restrictions.[E12][E22]

The video’s captions describe Canadian truckers opposing a vaccine mandate and subsequent copycat protests against Covid-19 restrictions worldwide; the protests, rather than the restrictions, are described as inspired by the convoy.[E12] Its images depict demonstrations, while the transcribed interview expresses opposition and calls for solidarity without measuring public opinion.[E16][E17][E11]

The external Washington Post report likewise describes Canadian protests inspiring demonstrations elsewhere, supporting the narrower account of international imitation in early 2022.[E22]

A worldwide decline in support, its magnitude, and any causal effect of the convoy remain unverified: the evidence obtained does not supply comparable public-opinion measurements across countries and dates, so it also does not establish that support was stable or increasing.[E12][E22]

The claim is misleading on the evidence obtained: contemporaneous reporting records Google's statement that it promoted President Trump's 2018 State of the Union on its homepage, contradicting the alleged omission.[E17][E19]

The video says Google promoted Obama's addresses but stopped when Trump took office; its images depict an Obama promotion and blank promotional areas labelled 2017 and 2018.[E4][E5][E7][E9][E10] These images establish what the video presents, not the authenticity or capture dates of the depicted homepages.[E13]

External reporting documents Trump circulating the accusation and Google publicly disputing it.[E16][E17][E18] The strongest supported conclusion concerns the disputed 2018 omission: a contemporaneous archived homepage was not independently verified, and the evidence does not establish a comprehensive promotion history across both administrations, times or locations.[E17][E19]

The claim is misleading: the policy announcement is supported, but the video identifies the speaker as Transport Secretary Grant Shapps MP, not Health Minister Jane Doe.[E15][E19]

The video's speech announces the removal of testing and paperwork, while its captions specify that remaining COVID travel measures for UK arrivals will end on 18 March.[E11][E12]

The external government announcement, dated 14 March 2022, specifies removal of remaining UK international travel restrictions from 4am Friday 18 March, including Passenger Locator Forms and testing for arrivals.[E19][E23] Subsequent government statistics record that testing and Passenger Locator Form requirements were removed on 18 March 2022 irrespective of vaccination status.[E20]

The supported scope is UK arrival requirements in March 2022, not worldwide travel rules or all domestic COVID measures.[E19][E20] “This week” fits the historical announcement's week, but the title's circulation date and the video's recording and original upload dates were not established, so its relative timing cannot be verified.[E19][E23]

The title is misleading on the evidence obtained: it emphasises rapid spread, while the video's recognised captions describe Deltacron as remaining a very rare variant.[E11] The captions report cases in France, the Netherlands, Denmark, the US and the UK; these are the video's claims, not independent confirmation.[E11] The examined images show a presenter speaking indoors, rather than case data or public health operations.[E7][E15]

External reporting describes detections in the US and Europe and attributes concern to WHO, but geographic detection alone does not establish rapid transmission; WHO's purported warning and a specific public health response were not independently verified.[E18] WHO's 22 March 2022 overview reports a 7% increase in overall weekly COVID-19 cases, not Deltacron-specific growth.[E19]

The evidence does not establish Deltacron's transmission rate or increased severity, so those claims remain unverified rather than disproved.[E11][E18] Video assessment relied on recognised captions and sampled images; speech transcription failed and intervening footage was not fully examined.[E11][E14][E7][E15] This conclusion concerns the March 2022 reporting context, not current circulation or risk; the video's publication date was not confirmed.[E19]

The claim is false: the video and external reporting describe more than 100 referrals for fixed penalty notices, contradicting the title’s assertion of no referrals.[E17][E21]

The video’s visible banner says more than 100 referrals have been made in relation to Partygate; its automated speech transcript likewise reports referrals and additional fines for breaches of COVID regulations at Whitehall and Downing Street.[E17][E11]

Separately, the Seychelles Broadcasting Corporation quotes the Metropolitan Police investigation as having “made more than 100 referrals for fixed penalty notices” and reports more than 50 additional fines.[E21]

This verdict concerns the announcement represented in the video: the police statement itself was not obtained, the audio account relies on automated transcription, and referrals, issued notices and individual recipients should not be treated as interchangeable counts.[E11][E21]

This establishes the title’s geographical misrepresentation; it does not establish whether separate U.S. protests occurred, whether they opposed new regulations, or whether their scale was unprecedented.[E11][E20][E22] Exact filming locations and dates of individual shots were not independently verified, and sampled images do not establish everything between them.[E15][E16][E19]
